cards.scenario: S3 data rarely read after 180 days, must be retrieved within 6 hours. MOST cost-effective?
cards.ok: S3 Intelligent-Tiering Archive Access tier
cards.bad: Intelligent-Tiering Deep Archive Access tier
cards.why: Deep Archive Access can take up to 12 h. Match the SLA first, then the cheapest tier.

cards.scenario: Lambda functions share hardcoded RDS credentials. Improve security, LEAST development effort.
cards.ok: Secrets Manager with managed rotation
cards.bad: Parameter Store + EventBridge-driven custom rotation
cards.why: Parameter Store has no native RDS rotation — you'd build it yourself.

cards.scenario: Organizations: CCoE must enforce daily EBS backups consistently across all accounts; MOST reliable.
cards.ok: Organizations backup policy driving AWS Backup plans
cards.bad: Backup policy using Data Lifecycle Manager
cards.why: Org backup policies are an AWS Backup feature; DLM is per-account lifecycle.

cards.scenario: Multi-Region API Gateway: reroute automatically on full AND partial failures from CloudWatch metrics.
cards.ok: Route 53 ARC routing controls driven by alarms + Lambda
cards.bad: Route 53 Evaluate Target Health
cards.why: Evaluate Target Health sees only the endpoint record, not partial failures inside the microservices.

cards.scenario: Two EC2 behind an ALB slow down at unexpected sales peaks, no time pattern.
cards.ok: Target tracking scaling on ALBRequestCountPerTarget
cards.bad: Scheduled scaling for the peak hours
cards.why: Scheduled actions only fit predictable peaks.

cards.scenario: Multi-AZ app with one NAT gateway and DynamoDB tables. Increase resilience.
cards.ok: One NAT gateway per AZ
cards.bad: DynamoDB global tables
cards.why: DynamoDB is already multi-AZ. The single NAT gateway is the zonal SPOF.

cards.scenario: Tightly coupled HPC: increase network throughput, reduce latency. Pick the instance/AMI settings.
cards.ok: EFA-capable instances + cluster placement group (single AZ) + disable hyperthreading, HVM AMI
cards.bad: Paravirtual (PV) AMI
cards.why: PV is legacy and slower. Disabling hyperthreading helps tightly coupled HPC.

cards.scenario: Protect S3, EBS, EFS, RDS, Volume Gateway against a Regional outage, LEAST overhead.
cards.ok: AWS Backup plan with cross-Region copy to a vault in another Region
cards.bad: AWS Backup plus RDS cross-Region read replicas
cards.why: Replicas aren't backups and add overhead; AWS Backup already covers RDS.

cards.scenario: Deploy Config rules to nearly all accounts incl. management, exclude a few; members must not modify them.
cards.ok: Organization conformance pack via a delegated admin
cards.bad: StackSets plus drift detection
cards.why: Drift detection only detects changes; it doesn't prevent them.

cards.scenario: Runbook describes install and config steps. LEAST overhead, must allow future changes.
cards.ok: CloudFormation for infra + user data / cfn-init for install; change via stack updates
cards.bad: CloudFormation for infra, keep manual runbook steps for software
cards.why: Automate the whole runbook, not just the infrastructure.

cards.scenario: WorkSpaces users sign in with on-prem AD; credentials must not be stored outside the company.
cards.ok: AD Connector (proxy, no caching)
cards.bad: AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust
cards.why: Managed AD is a real directory — credentials then live in AWS.

cards.scenario: A/B test two site versions in two S3 buckets behind CloudFront; users must not notice.
cards.ok: Lambda@Edge on origin request picks the origin (cookie/request attributes)
cards.bad: Path-based cache behaviors + redirects
cards.why: Different paths and redirects are visible to users.

cards.scenario: Millions of unencrypted S3 objects, many apps use the bucket. Find PII, encrypt, LEAST effort.
cards.ok: Default encryption + S3 Inventory + Batch Operations copy-in-place; Macie finds PII
cards.bad: Copy everything to a new encrypted bucket
cards.why: A new bucket forces every application to change bucket names.

cards.scenario: Aurora Global Database: local low-latency reads with read-after-write consistency, test DR.
cards.ok: Write forwarding on the secondary + managed (planned) failover for DR tests
cards.bad: Read from the secondary, write to the primary
cards.why: Secondary reads may be stale and break read-after-write.

cards.scenario: Remove open SSH/RDP and bastions, log commands per session, keep port forwarding.
cards.ok: Systems Manager Session Manager (close port 22, logs to S3/CloudWatch)
cards.bad: Client VPN or EC2 Instance Connect
cards.why: VPN keeps SSH open, no session logs; Instance Connect still needs port 22.

cards.scenario: AWS Batch jobs need a custom AMI, jobs are restartable. Reduce management overhead and cost.
cards.ok: Batch managed compute environment on EC2 Spot with the custom AMI
cards.bad: Batch on Fargate Spot
cards.why: Fargate cannot use a custom AMI. Restartable jobs tolerate Spot interruptions.

cards.scenario: 500 workloads in separate accounts; security and infra teams; a few unique workloads. Account structure?
cards.ok: Separate Log Archive, Security Tooling and Audit accounts plus an Exceptions OU
cards.bad: One central security account for logging, tooling and audit
cards.why: Separating them limits blast radius.

cards.scenario: Grid computing: timeouts between instances, adding instances didn't help. LEAST effort fix?
cards.ok: Relaunch the nodes from the AMI into a cluster placement group
cards.bad: Enable ENA on the instances
cards.why: Current instances already use ENA. The problem is inter-node latency.

cards.scenario: SQS workers on EC2 don't scale well. MOST scalable scaling metric?
cards.ok: Target tracking on backlog per instance (messages ÷ in-service instances, custom metric)
cards.bad: Scale on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
cards.why: Queue depth doesn't change in proportion to fleet size. FIFO + dedup removes duplicates.

cards.scenario: On-prem apps on several servers share static files over NFS; move to S3, one copy.
cards.ok: S3 File Gateway
cards.bad: Volume Gateway (iSCSI)
cards.why: Volume Gateway stores block volumes, not S3 objects, and can't be shared like NFS.

cards.scenario: SQS queue shared across org accounts. Identify principals outside the org that can access it.
cards.ok: IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as zone of trust
cards.bad: CloudTrail data events
cards.why: Who CAN access = policy analysis; CloudTrail only shows who DID call.

cards.scenario: Firewall Manager + Network Firewall strict order: allow SSH from trusted CIDRs, deny everything else.
cards.ok: Allow rule at the lowest priority number, deny-all after
cards.bad: Allow rule given the highest order number
cards.why: Rules evaluate from the lowest number; deny-all first blocks trusted SSH too.

cards.scenario: HR and Recruiting share SCP requirements; Recruiting needs stricter ones. Avoid duplicate effort.
cards.ok: Nest the Recruiting OU under the shared OU; move accounts between OUs
cards.bad: Remove accounts from the org and re-invite them
cards.why: SCPs inherit down nested OUs; moving accounts is cheap.

cards.scenario: Projected EC2 cost may exceed budget. Notify the CFO; LOWEST risk of overspending.
cards.ok: Budgets forecast alert plus a Budgets action that stops instances
cards.bad: Budgets alert to an operator who stops instances manually
cards.why: Automation beats a human step; manual delay leaves overspend risk.

cards.scenario: DynamoDB on-demand, bursts, a few hot keys read repeatedly. Cut cost, LEAST overhead.
cards.ok: DAX for hot keys + provisioned capacity with auto scaling (or reserved capacity)
cards.bad: DAX + Savings Plans
cards.why: Savings Plans never cover DynamoDB (EC2/Fargate/Lambda/SageMaker only).

cards.scenario: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 keys, needed only in business hours, HA. MOST cost-effective?
cards.ok: CloudHSM multi-AZ cluster; delete/restore from backup outside hours
cards.bad: KMS key with scheduled disable/enable
cards.why: Exam treats KMS as Level 2. (Real AWS: KMS reached Level 3 in 2023 — answer CloudHSM.)

cards.scenario: PHP LAMP app, developer with little AWS skill, stable traffic, predictable pricing.
cards.ok: Amazon Lightsail
cards.bad: Elastic Beanstalk + DynamoDB
cards.why: Pay-per-resource pricing and a new NoSQL DB break the asks.

cards.scenario: Existing bucket with default settings; objects must not be deleted or overwritten for 5 years.
cards.ok: New bucket with Object Lock compliance mode; move the objects
cards.bad: Enable Object Lock on the existing bucket
cards.why: Exam key assumes Object Lock only on new buckets (real AWS allows existing since 2023).

cards.scenario: SLA 99.5%, minimize changes and cost; remote users find the desktop client slow.
cards.ok: Keep RDS single-AZ; stream the client with AppStream 2.0
cards.bad: Add RDS Multi-AZ + ElastiCache
cards.why: Single-AZ already meets 99.5%; a cache doesn't fix a slow remote desktop client.

cards.scenario: Dev DynamoDB provisioned for peak, write-heavy, 2x weekend peak. Optimize cost.
cards.ok: On-demand capacity only
cards.bad: On-demand capacity + DAX
cards.why: DAX caches reads only — it never helps writes. No hot data = pure extra cost.

cards.scenario: Interface endpoints in private subnets, private IPs only, connections fail. Configuration fix?
cards.ok: Endpoint ENI security group allows 443 from the VPC (+ private DNS)
cards.bad: Add a route table entry for the endpoint
cards.why: Interface endpoints are ENIs reached via DNS; only gateway endpoints use route tables.

cards.scenario: EKS stateless pods, highly variable load. Optimize node resilience.
cards.ok: Topology spread constraints across AZs + node groups in multiple AZs
cards.bad: Cluster Autoscaler with under-provisioning
cards.why: Resilience = survive an AZ failure; autoscaler sizing is capacity, not fault tolerance.

cards.scenario: S3 behind CloudFront: encrypt in transit and at rest.
cards.ok: Default encryption + bucket policy denying unencrypted PutObject + CloudFront HTTP→HTTPS redirect
cards.bad: aws:SecureTransport condition in S3 ACLs
cards.why: ACLs can't hold condition keys — only bucket policies can.

cards.scenario: ECS behind ALB suffers attacks causing outages. Prevent attacks, MOST cost-effective.
cards.ok: CloudFront + WAF web ACL + custom-header origin lock on the ALB
cards.bad: Auto scaling + DAX
cards.why: Scaling and caching absorb load; they don't stop attacks or bypass to the ALB.

cards.scenario: PII on SSE-S3 today; security team must manage keys for current and future objects.
cards.ok: SSE-KMS customer managed key + deny unencrypted PutObject + re-copy existing objects
cards.bad: SSE-S3 with a customer managed key
cards.why: SSE-S3 keys are always AWS-owned; that option is impossible.

cards.scenario: Track cost per project and per environment; teams may use only pre-approved services.
cards.ok: Cost allocation tags plus Service Catalog portfolios
cards.bad: Custom budgets per project
cards.why: Budgets alert on thresholds; they don't attribute cost. Tags do.

cards.scenario: NLB with instance-id targets, targets healthy, but office users can't connect.
cards.ok: Allow the office CIDR in the EC2 security group
cards.bad: Allow the NLB subnets in the EC2 security group
cards.why: Instance-id targets preserve the client IP. Healthy targets = health check already open.

cards.scenario: Existing 10 Gbps DX with one private VIF needs redundancy; also reach a VPC in a second Region.
cards.ok: Second DX to the same Region plus a Direct Connect gateway
cards.bad: New DX connection to the second Region
cards.why: That adds a path to another VPC, not redundancy; the DX gateway is global.

cards.scenario: 15 GB/day of statistics in S3 queried by Athena with date ranges; optimal performance.
cards.ok: Parquet/ORC with date partitions
cards.bad: A separate bucket per date range
cards.why: Partitions prune scanned data for date queries.

cards.scenario: Move an on-prem VMware app to EC2, preserving software and configuration.
cards.ok: Export OVF to S3, then VM Import
cards.bad: DataSync to an FSx for Windows datastore
cards.why: A VM isn't a file share; VM Import keeps it as-is.

cards.scenario: Batch scripts → serverless microservices, each step takes seconds. MOST cost-effective orchestration?
cards.ok: Lambda functions orchestrated by Step Functions
cards.bad: Fargate containers orchestrated by Step Functions
cards.why: Seconds-long steps fit Lambda's 15 min; Fargate costs more. EventBridge is not an orchestrator.

cards.scenario: HA EC2 app: filter common exploits, send rejected requests to a third-party audit tool.
cards.ok: Multi-AZ ASG behind ALB + WAF managed rules + WAF logging to Firehose
cards.bad: WAF logs via CloudWatch + Lambda polling, no multi-AZ ASG
cards.why: Firehose can deliver WAF logs to third-party endpoints; HA needs a multi-AZ ASG.

cards.scenario: Expense app with Friday bursts; HA; LEAST operational overhead.
cards.ok: S3 + CloudFront front end, API Gateway + Lambda back end
cards.bad: ECS behind an ALB
cards.why: Containers still need cluster capacity management unless Fargate.

cards.scenario: Always-on production tier in two Regions, failover within 1 minute. Capacity purchase?
cards.ok: Active/passive ASG on zonal RIs + On-Demand, failover record with low TTL
cards.bad: Active/active on Spot instances
cards.why: Spot can be reclaimed — never for the always-on production baseline.

cards.scenario: Regional REST API hit by botnets; only a few known US companies call it twice daily. Minimum cost.
cards.ok: WAF IP allow-list on the API + usage plan and API key
cards.bad: CloudFront + WAF per-day rate-based rule
cards.why: Rate rules use short windows, not per day; CloudFront adds cost.

cards.scenario: Single Direct Connect for business-critical traffic. MOST resilient connectivity?
cards.ok: Second DX connection, different carrier/location, same Region
cards.bad: VPN backup or a new DX to another Region
cards.why: VPN is low-bandwidth backup; DX to another Region isn't redundancy for this one.
cards.src: Neal A Q56, Neal C Q31, Udemy2 Q67

cards.scenario: Move 25 TB to S3 fast: 1 Gbps internet, 500 Mbps Direct Connect.
cards.ok: S3 Transfer Acceleration over the 1 Gbps link
cards.bad: Snowball
cards.why: ~2-3 days online beats shipping; Snowball pays off past ~1 week.

cards.scenario: DynamoDB auto scaling at 70%; predictable spike to 300% causes throttling.
cards.ok: Application Auto Scaling scheduled action to raise capacity before the spike
cards.bad: Retry throttled writes from a DLQ / rely on target tracking
cards.why: Target tracking and step scaling react after the breach; predictable spikes need capacity ready.

cards.scenario: Serverless global app: low latency + baseline DDoS protection for S3 content.
cards.ok: CloudFront (Shield Standard included) in front of S3
cards.bad: WAF web ACL for DDoS
cards.why: WAF filters L7 rules (SQLi/XSS); baseline DDoS comes free with CloudFront.

cards.scenario: 350 remote staff need full Windows/Linux desktops with on-prem AD and MFA.
cards.ok: WorkSpaces + AD Connector + RADIUS MFA
cards.bad: AppStream 2.0
cards.why: AppStream streams apps, not full desktops.

cards.scenario: Mobile app with custom authentication must get IAM role credentials. Pick the federation path.
cards.ok: OIDC IdP + Cognito identity pool, or SAML assertion via an IAM SAML IdP
cards.bad: LDAP connector + API Gateway Lambda authorizer issuing JWTs
cards.why: Authorizers only authorize API calls; they never issue AWS credentials.

cards.scenario: Security team wants all identities central across prod/test accounts.
cards.ok: IAM users in one identity account; roles in target accounts trust that account
cards.bad: IAM users in every account restricted with SCPs
cards.why: SCPs only restrict, never grant; users stay scattered.

cards.scenario: Only the management account may buy Reserved Instances, for all current and future member accounts.
cards.ok: Deny SCP attached at the root
cards.bad: Deny SCP on a new OU holding the current accounts
cards.why: Root covers every present and future member; SCPs never affect the management account.

cards.scenario: 99.9% SLA, or HA across three AZs, for an app with PostgreSQL. Users in Europe/US.
cards.ok: One Region: Aurora writer + replicas in other AZs; CloudFront for global latency
cards.bad: Two Regions with Aurora Global Database
cards.why: Aurora Global is cross-Region DR — overbuilt for a single-Region SLA.

cards.scenario: Check service quotas every 15 minutes and alert at 80% utilization.
cards.ok: CloudWatch alarm on AWS/Usage with SERVICE_QUOTA() to SNS
cards.bad: AWS Budgets alert
cards.why: Budgets tracks cost and usage spend, never quotas.

cards.scenario: Detect an API action (CreateUser, public-read PutObject), notify and auto-remediate.
cards.ok: CloudTrail event → EventBridge rule → Step Functions/Lambda remediate + SNS notify
cards.bad: CloudTrail alone or S3 event notifications
cards.why: CloudTrail doesn't notify; S3 events can't filter on ACL.

cards.scenario: Serverless comments app (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) must show new comments in real time.
cards.ok: AWS AppSync GraphQL subscriptions over WebSockets
cards.bad: CloudFront caching of the API responses
cards.why: Cached comments aren't new — real time needs push, not caching or polling.

cards.scenario: RDS Multi-AZ failover 40 s → under 20 s, keep connections alive, queue writes.
cards.ok: RDS Proxy + Aurora with Aurora Replicas
cards.bad: Redis cache + RDS MySQL read replicas
cards.why: Caches can't queue writes; RDS replicas don't give fast failover.

cards.scenario: One EC2 instance (RI + On-Demand) must survive an AZ outage. MOST cost-effective?
cards.ok: Spot Fleet mixing On-Demand baseline and Spot across AZs behind an ALB
cards.bad: Auto Scaling group of On-Demand instances across AZs
cards.why: All On-Demand works but costs more. All-Spot risks interruption.

cards.scenario: CloudFront default origin = ALB; S3 static assets with OAC return 404.
cards.ok: Add an S3 origin + a path-pattern cache behavior in CloudFront
cards.bad: ALB listener path rule forwarding to S3
cards.why: OAC lets only CloudFront read S3; an ALB cannot forward to S3.

cards.scenario: One data center needs low-latency links to VPCs in US East and US West.
cards.ok: One DX connection + Direct Connect gateway with a VGW per VPC (private VIFs)
cards.bad: A separate DX connection per Region
cards.why: A DX gateway is global — one connection reaches VPCs in many Regions.

cards.scenario: Lambda metadata extraction takes 45 min per photo. Split by metadata type to cut time.
cards.ok: Step Functions: Parallel state per metadata type, plus a workflow iterating over photos
cards.bad: Lambda sends photos to SQS as the Step Functions input
cards.why: SQS cannot directly start a Step Functions workflow.

cards.scenario: KMS-encrypted Redshift: RPO 24 h, RTO 1 h, survive a Regional outage.
cards.ok: Cross-Region snapshot copy; snapshot copy grant for a key in the DESTINATION Region
cards.bad: Redshift replication to a cluster in another Region / grant in source Region
cards.why: Redshift has no cross-Region replication. KMS keys are Regional.

cards.scenario: gp2 3 TB volume needs +3,000 IOPS per instance; MOST cost-efficient.
cards.ok: Grow the gp2 volume by 1 TB (or move to gp3)
cards.bad: Move the data to EFS
cards.why: gp2 = 3 IOPS per GiB; EFS adds cost and no IOPS guarantee.

cards.scenario: Serverless upload app, users in many Regions, low latency. API Gateway Regional + S3 today.
cards.ok: API Gateway edge-optimized endpoint + S3 Transfer Acceleration
cards.bad: Global Accelerator in front of CloudFront
cards.why: GA fronts ALB/NLB/EC2/EIP only — never CloudFront or S3.

cards.scenario: Serverless API returns 504 on image loads; DynamoDB fine; find the root cause.
cards.ok: X-Ray traces plus Lambda CloudWatch Logs
cards.bad: API Gateway execution logging
cards.why: Gateway logs confirm the 504, not where the time goes.

cards.scenario: Copy KMS-encrypted Redshift snapshots to another Region for DR.
cards.ok: Snapshot copy grant for a destination-Region key; enable copy in source
cards.bad: Copy grant in the source Region with the source key
cards.why: KMS keys are Regional; the grant must be in the destination.

cards.scenario: After a DDoS on EC2 + RDS serving static images, revamp security.
cards.ok: Route 53, CloudFront with static content on S3, WAF on CloudFront
cards.bad: WAF in front of the Auto Scaling group
cards.why: WAF attaches to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito; never EC2/ASG.

cards.scenario: Sensor data → DynamoDB, fully serverless, no manual capacity planning.
cards.ok: SQS + Lambda writing to DynamoDB (auto scaling)
cards.bad: Kinesis Data Firehose writing directly to DynamoDB
cards.why: DynamoDB is not a Firehose destination. KDS needs shard planning.

cards.scenario: Gaming leaderboard: in-memory, single-digit ms, highly available.
cards.ok: ElastiCache for Redis (sorted sets) or DynamoDB + DAX
cards.bad: Plain DynamoDB tables
cards.why: DynamoDB alone is disk-based, not in-memory.

cards.scenario: Detect an S3 object made public-read, alarm and auto-remediate.
cards.ok: CloudTrail data events plus EventBridge rule, then SNS and Lambda
cards.bad: S3 event notifications
cards.why: Event notifications can't filter by ACL, only event type and key prefix/suffix.

cards.scenario: Several data centers on private fiber need HA, high-bandwidth, multi-Region AWS connectivity.
cards.ok: Direct Connect at each DC from different providers
cards.bad: Direct Connect with a VPN backup
cards.why: VPN backup is low bandwidth; diverse DX gives HA plus bandwidth.

cards.scenario: Copy 140 TB monthly on-prem to S3 over an existing 10 Gbps DX with a private VIF; LEAST expensive.
cards.ok: Add a public VIF on the same DX
cards.bad: S3 gateway endpoint over the private VIF
cards.why: Gateway endpoints aren't reachable from on-prem; a public VIF reaches S3.
